items.headline: How Claude is accelerating protein design and analytical chemistry
items.dek: Claude (Mythos Preview and Opus 4.8) designed protein binders against 15 targets, and succeeded against 14 of them. Between 22% and 35% of its individual designs bound successfully, depending on the setup, compared to the 10-15% that is typical in protein design campaigns today.

items.headline: Anthropic says Claude designed protein binders for 14 of 15 targets
items.dek: Anthropic said its Claude AI models designed protein binders that succeeded against 14 of 15 targets in wet-lab testing. items.dek: Out of 1,320 designs, 354 bound their target, giving Claude an average hit rate of 26.8%. Only a single target yielded 0 binders. Compared to the results of our Protein Design Competitions, Claude's designs had noticeably higher success rates and would have won 5 out 6, yielding tighter binders.

facts.claim: Claude (Opus 4.8 and Mythos Preview) autonomously designed de novo protein binders against 15 analyzable targets and produced confirmed binders for 14 of them, with 354 of 1,320 designs binding (a 27% hit rate) - versus the 10-15% typical of protein-design campaigns.
facts.source: Anthropic, 'How Claude is accelerating protein design and analytical chemistry' + technical report

facts.claim: Among the designs Claude ranked FIRST for each target, 49% bound - i.e. its single top pick worked about half the time; the single-target campaign hit rate reached 35.1%.
facts.source: Anthropic / Claude Science technical report, Results and Fig. 2

facts.claim: Claude ran each 24- to 48-hour campaign autonomously from one ~16,000-word protocol prompt: it researched each target, chose epitopes, installed and ran open-source design tools, optimized in silico, and delivered 30 ranked designs per target - with no human input into any design decision (only non-technical restart messages after infrastructure failures).

On RBX1 - the subject of an open design competition where only 9 of 245 de novo designs bound - 28 of Claude's 90 designs bound, and its tightest hit reached a dissociation constant of 3.9 nM versus 45 nM for the competition's winning entry re-measured on the same plate.
facts.source: Anthropic / Claude Science technical report, Abstract

facts.claim: Anthropic frames the result as dual-use: 'The uplift provided by the increasingly autonomous research capabilities of AI models will undoubtedly speed the development of human therapies and fundamental scientific discoveries. However, such capabilities are also dual-use: without robust safety measures, they could enable bad actors to perform dangerous research, such as the development of bioweapons.' Protein design and other dual-use biology capabilities remain unavailable for general access in Claude Fable 5.
facts.source: Anthropic, 'How Claude is accelerating protein design and analytical chemistry'

facts.claim: Adaptyv Bio, the independent lab that physically made and tested the designs, concluded: 'Claude seems to have matched or even surpassed expert protein designers when it orchestrates openly available design tools,' and that Claude's designs 'would have won 5 out 6' of Adaptyv's past Protein Design Competitions.
facts.source: Adaptyv Bio, 'Case study: Benchmarking Claude's protein designs in the wet lab'

facts.claim: OpenAI's purpose-built biology model GPT-Rosalind-5.5 was judged to have 'met our threshold for High capability' in the Biological and Chemical domain under its Preparedness Framework (while below 'Critical'), and - unlike GPT-5.5 - 'is trained not to refuse sophisticated biology queries,' with vetted access to scientists and government partners as the primary safeguard.

On a fully held-out SecureBio virology-troubleshooting set (multi-select), GPT-5.5 Pro scored 55.34% and GPT-Rosalind-5.5 51.2%; on an expert-written, uncontaminated wet-lab TroubleshootingBench, GPT-Rosalind-5.5 reached 53.31% pass@1 (vs GPT-5.5's 44.1%).

A mid-2026 survey of bio-uplift research reports that novices with LLMs were 4.16x more accurate than controls across 8 in-silico benchmarks (Zhang, Knight et al. 2026), while real wet-lab novice-uplift RCTs remain non-significant (Hong et al. 2026, n=153: a 1.42-fold, non-significant improvement) - and warns 'Experts will be the first group uplifted to access catastrophic bio capabilities; novice uplift will remain a late signal.'
facts.source: Humam Aziz, 'The State of Bio-Uplift Research in Mid-2026', EA Forum (survey citing primary sources)
